title: How to use this package
goal: The company knows which chapters it needs, who owns them, and when they are reviewed.
summary: The SharePoint Online Governance package is a set of standalone chapters from which the company selects those it needs, fills in its details, and approves them as its own internal policies. This chapter explains how the package is built, how to read levels and licenses, how to adopt chapters, and how to keep them up to date.

sections.title: 1. Purpose and scope
sections.html:
1. Purpose and scope

SharePoint Online works without rules only for a short time. Sites get created and orphaned, permissions swell, nobody watches external sharing, content ages, and search and AI assistants then return the clutter that sits in the tenant. Governance is not a brake: it is a set of decisions about who owns what, what is allowed, and how it is verified. The package prepares these decisions so that the company can adopt them in weeks, not months.

The package covers SharePoint Online and OneDrive, including their links to Microsoft Teams, Microsoft Entra, Microsoft Purview, and Microsoft 365 Copilot. It does not cover the administration of Exchange, Windows, or the network.

sections.title: 2. Rules
sections.html:
2. Rules

  • P-00-01Basic The company maintains adopted chapters as internal policies: each has an owner, an approval, an effective date, and a next review date.
  • P-00-02Basic Adopted chapters are published in one place (the governance site on the intranet or Managed Documents), not sent out by email.
  • P-00-03Basic Chapters are adopted in full. A deviation from a rule is recorded in the exception register with a justification and an end date, not by silently deleting the sentence.
  • P-00-04Basic Each chapter is reviewed at the latest after 12 months, or when a platform change affects it.
  • P-00-05Standard The selection of chapters is based on the maturity assessment (the 18-area questionnaire) and on the gap against the target level for the company's size.

sections.title: 4. Procedures
sections.html:
4. Procedures

4.1 How the package is built

Chapters GOV-01 to GOV-23 are arranged in seven pillars: Foundation, Structure, Trust, Experience, Value, Operations, People. Appendices A to F carry what is not written into policies: the tenant settings baseline, templates and checklists, the RACI matrix, the glossary, the rollout plan, and the regulatory mapping. The Chapter list states for each chapter its audience, owner, and recommended level by company size; the index leads from a term to the chapter.

Every chapter has the same skeleton: summary, document header, purpose and scope, numbered rules, roles and activities, procedures, Microsoft 365 settings, verification and metrics, templates, related chapters and sources. A rule has the code P-<chapter>-<sequence>, for example P-10-02, and can be referenced from other policies, from the exception register, and from an audit.

4.2 Levels and company size

Every chapter distinguishes three levels:

  • Basic – the necessary minimum that one administrator can handle without additional tools.
  • Standard – written rules, regular reviews, partial automation.
  • Advanced – full automation, measurement, integration with other systems.

A rule marked Basic applies to everyone; a Standard rule applies from the Standard level; an Advanced rule only at the Advanced level. The recommended level by company size (S up to 100 users, M up to 1,000, L above 1,000) is in the header of every chapter and in the Chapter list. The Trust pillar always targets at least Standard regardless of size. A level is an ambition, not a state; raising it by two levels at once does not pay off.

4.3 Licenses

The chapters do not assume any specific Microsoft 365 plan. Every setting and report carries a license label:

LabelWhat it means
M365 baseAny plan with SharePoint Online
Entra ID P1Business Premium, Microsoft 365 E3/E5: Conditional Access, group naming policy, group expiration policy
Entra ID P2Microsoft 365 E5, Entra ID Governance: access reviews, PIM
Purview (E3)Manual sensitivity labels, basic DLP, retention policies, 180-day audit
Purview (E5)Automatic labeling, retention labels with disposition, records, 1-year audit, DLP for Copilot
SAMSharePoint Advanced Management: at least one Microsoft 365 Copilot license in the tenant, the SAM Plan 1 add-on, or Microsoft 365 E7
CopilotMicrosoft 365 Copilot license for the user
M365 Backup · M365 ArchivePaid by data volume
Power Platform · Defender (Plan 1) · Defender (E5)Premium connectors and Dataverse; Safe Attachments for SharePoint in Defender for Office 365 Plan 1; Defender for Cloud Apps in E5

A setting without the required license is skipped and recorded in the exception register as "not licensed" so that it is visible at the next review.

4.4 Adopting a chapter

  1. The governance lead selects the chapter based on the maturity assessment and assigns an owner (the role in the header).
  2. The owner completes the header: company name, approver, effective date, next review. The owner fills in the details in square brackets in the text.
  3. The owner goes through the rules and marks which apply from when. A rule the company does not adopt is recorded in the exception register with a reason and an end date.
  4. The SharePoint administrator applies the settings from section 5 and verifies the metrics from section 6.
  5. The sponsor approves the chapter; the governance lead publishes it on the governance site or in Managed Documents and notifies the affected roles.
  6. The owner records the next review date in the review schedule.

4.5 Updating the package

The package version has the form year and month, for example 2026.09; each chapter has its own version. Changes to the Microsoft 365 platform are reflected in the chapters in new versions with a summary of changes. On an update, the owner compares the adopted version with the new one, takes over the changes, and adds the review date. The chapter is not rewritten as a whole; only the affected rules and settings change.

Tools

Microsoft 365: a communication site for governance, SharePoint lists for the exception register and the review schedule. EP365: Managed Documents releases approved chapters to employees with acknowledgment and an audit trail; Atlas shows which rules of the adopted chapters the tenant meets, and the maturity assessment suggests which chapters to adopt first.
